proposal_topic_title: ML for Public-Health Data Security under Coordinated APT Attack
proposal_topic_intro:
Public-health data systems aggregate sensitive individual records that are high-value targets for advanced persistent threat actors. Contact-tracing databases, hospital imaging archives, and vaccination registries each present distinct attack surfaces while sharing a common need for privacy-preserving access controls.

Two of the four participating labs (Alpha and Gamma) contribute directly to autonomous network defence under APT conditions. Beta's work on privacy-preserving contact tracing and immunity passport non-discrimination addresses the public-health data layer. Delta's deep RL network defence and adversarial contextual bandit research provides additional ML methodology.

participating_pis.research_summary: Alpha leads Lab-Alpha, applying reinforcement learning to network defence. The lab built RL agents that defend against advanced persistent threats (APTs), investigated LLM copyright tracing in fine-tuned models, and developed multi-agent deep RL for communication resilience in drone networks under attack.

Beta leads Lab-Beta, working on privacy-preserving public-health technology and autonomous network defence. Lab projects include privacy-preserving contact tracing for COVID-19, immunity passport non-discrimination design, and deep RL backdoor detection for network-defence policies.

Gamma leads Lab-Gamma, specialising in malicious-activity detection and autonomous network defence. The lab built Bilbo, a CNN-LSTM hybrid for domain generation algorithm (DGA) detection, and an RL agent defending against APTs in simulated network environments.

Delta leads Lab-Delta, bridging cybersecurity, financial technology, and ML. The lab developed market-fairness frameworks for equity-exchange order matching, a fast-payment protocol for permissionless blockchains, and autonomous network defence using deep RL against sophisticated cyber threats.
